children.text: tataśca tatpratipakṣa karasyāṅguṣṭhamūle yā dhamanī jīvasākṣiṇī
children.translated_text: And then, at the root of the thumb of the opposite hand, there is the artery that bears witness to life.

children.text: tacceṣṭayā sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ jñeyaṃ kāyasya paṇḍitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: By its movement, the wise should know the body's ease and distress.
When <s>marut</s> (vāta) is aggravated, the pulse assumes the motion of a leech or a snake.
When pitta is aggravated, it has the motion of a sparrow, crow, or frog.
When śleṣman is aggravated, it assumes the motion of a goose or a pigeon.
In a combined disorder it has the gait of a quail, partridge, or vartī bird.
Sometimes it moves slowly, and sometimes it flows with speed.
It should be known as due to the aggravation of two doṣas; and when displaced from its place, it kills.

children.text: sthitvā sthitvā calati yā sā smṛtā prāṇanāśinī
children.translated_text: The pulse that moves after stopping again and again is remembered as destructive of life.

children.text: atikṣīṇā ca śītā ca jīvitaṃ hantyasaṃśayam ||
children.translated_text: If it is extremely feeble and cold, it undoubtedly destroys life.
Through the aggravation of fever, the artery becomes warm and rapid.
Through desire and anger it flows swiftly; when overwhelmed by worry and fear it is feeble.
In one whose digestive fire is weak and whose bodily constituents are depleted, the pulse becomes very slow.
When full of blood, it becomes slightly warm and heavy; when with <s>āma</s> (undigested matter), it is still heavier.
In one whose digestive fire is blazing, it flows lightly and is considered rapid.

children.text: sukhitasya sthirā jñeyā tathā balavatī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: In a happy person it should be known as steady, and it is also remembered as strong.
In a hungry person it is restless, while in a satisfied person it flows steadily.
Gold, silver, brass, copper, lead, tin, and sharp iron
are to be understood as the seven metals; therefore the wise man should purify them.
One should heat leaves of gold, silver, brass, copper, and iron in fire.
When they are heated again and again, one should quench them in oil, buttermilk, and sour gruel,

children.text: gomūtre ca kulatthānāṃ kaṣāye ca tridhā tridhā
children.translated_text: and also in cow's urine and in a decoction of horse gram, three times in each.
Thus the purification of metals beginning with gold is properly produced.

children.text: nāgavaṅgau prataptau ca gālitau tau niṣiñcayet
children.translated_text: Lead and tin, once heated and melted, should be quenched

children.text: tridhā tridhā viśuddhiḥ syādravidugdhena ca tridhā ||
children.translated_text: three times each; purification is obtained, and also three times with the milk of the arka plant.
One should grind mercury twice the amount of gold together with an acid substance.
One should place sulfur equal to that pellet below and above it.
Then one should seal the pellet in a firm covered earthen saucer.
With thirty forest cow-dung cakes one should give heatings; in this way, fourteen heatings are prescribed.

children.text: nirutthaṃ jāyate bhasma gandho deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: A non-revivable bhasma is produced; sulfur should be added again and again.
Into melted gold one should put lead in a sixteenth part.

children.text: cūrṇayitvā tathāmlena ghṛṣṭvā kṛtvā ca golakam
children.translated_text: After pulverizing it, grinding it with an acid, and making a pellet,
one should add sulfur equal to the pellet, both below and above.
Having placed it in a sealed earthen-saucer container, one should heat it with thirty forest cow-dung cakes.
Thus, with seven heatings, gold becomes a non-revivable bhasma.
Having ground it with the juices of kāñcanāra and with a collyrium-like mixture of equal mercury and sulfur,
one should smear gold leaves with an equal measure.
One should prepare a pair of crucibles with pastes of kāñcanāra bark.
Having placed the pellet in that sealed container, one should cook it in a sealed clay crucible.

children.text: nidhāya saṃdhirodhaṃ ca kṛtvā saṃśoṣya kokilaiḥ
children.translated_text: After placing it, sealing the joint, and drying it, with cow-dung cakes
one should make a very fierce fire; in this way one should give three heatings.
A non-revivable bhasma is produced, and it may be used in all operations.
By the method using kāñcanāra, lāṅgalī destroys gold.
Just as jvālāmukhī destroys it, so also does manaḥśilā.
Of powders of śilā and sindūra, in equal amount, with the milk of arka,
one should give exactly seven impregnations and dry it again and again.

children.text: tatastu gālite hemni kalko'yaṃ dīyate samaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then this paste is added in equal measure to melted gold.
One should blow it again very strongly, so that the paste melts.
In this way the paste should be applied three times; the death of gold results.
Alternatively, one should smear gold leaves with pigeon droppings or with those produced by hens,
and should put them between layers of those substances.
Having taken an equal amount of sulfur powder in a sealed pair of earthen saucers,
one should give a kukkuṭa heating with five cow-dung cakes.
Thus one should give nine heatings, and the tenth should be a great heating.
It should be given with thirty forest cow-dung cakes; gold bhasma is produced.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ ca bhavetsvādu tiktaṃ snigdhaṃ himaṃ guru
children.translated_text: Gold is sweet, bitter, unctuous, cooling, and heavy.
It produces intellect, learning, and memory; it removes poison and is a rejuvenating remedy.
One part of tālaka should be ground with jambīra juice or with some acid substance.
With that, one should smear three parts of silver leaves.
Having placed it in a crucible container, sealed it, one should heat it with thirty forest cow-dung cakes.

children.text: samuddhṛtya punastālaṃ dattvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: After taking it out, one should again add tāla, seal it, and cook it in a heating.
Thus, by fourteen heatings, silver becomes bhasma.
Mākṣika, ground with the milk of snuhī, should be used to smear them.
According to the method of tālaka, the wise man should treat the silver leaves.
He should heat them with fourteen heatings; silver becomes bhasma.
Sulfur ground with the milk of arka should be used to smear
equal leaves of copper, purified repeatedly with acidic liquids.
Then, having placed it in a crucible container, one should heat it with a gajapuṭa.
By just two such heatings copper certainly becomes bhasma.
Brass too, just like copper, certainly goes to the state of bhasma.
As with the milk of arka, goat's milk may be used, and likewise the milk of nirguṇḍikā.
For the killing of copper, brass, and bell-metal, an equal combination with sulfur is used.
Having made fine copper leaves, the wise man should steam them
for three days with an acid substance; then he should put them into a mortar.
After adding mercury equal to a quarter part, he should grind it with an acid for one watch.
Then, taking out the leaves, he should smear them with twice as much
sulfur ground with acid, and should make a pellet of it.

children.text: tataḥ piṣṭvā ca mīnākṣīṃ cāṅgerīṃ vā punarnavām ||
children.translated_text: Then, after grinding mīnākṣī, cāṅgerī, or punarnavā,
one should smear the outside of the pellet with that paste to a thickness of one finger.

children.text: dhṛtvā tadgolakaṃ bhāṇḍe śarāveṇa ca rodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed that pellet in a vessel, one should close it with an earthen saucer.
Then, after filling it with sand, ashes, salt, and water,
and after applying a seal at the mouth of the vessel, one should cook it on the hearth.
With a fire gradually increased, it should be cooked properly for four watches.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out and grind it with the juices of sūraṇa.
For one day one should make it into a pellet and smear it with half as much sulfur.

children.text: saghṛtena tato mūṣāṃ puṭe gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Then, with ghee, one should cook the crucible in a gajapuṭa heating.

children.text: svāṅgaśītaṃ samuddhṛtya mṛtaṃ tāmraṃ śubhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out; the copper, having become dead, will be good.

children.text: vāntiṃ bhrāntiṃ klamaṃ mūrcchāṃ na karoti kadācana ||
children.translated_text: It never causes vomiting, dizziness, fatigue, or fainting.
Through repeated smearing with śilā ground with the juice of tāmbūlī,
lead, with thirty-two heatings, becomes non-revivable and reaches the state of bhasma.
One should add powder of the bark of aśvattha and ciñcā in a quarter part.
Into melted lead in an earthen vessel one should put it and stir it with an iron ladle.
In one watch it becomes bhasma; one should add an equal amount of manaḥśilā.
Having ground the two with kāñjika, one should cook them with a strong heating.

children.text: svāṅgaśītaṃ punaḥ piṣṭvā śilayā kāñjikena ca ||
children.translated_text: When it has cooled by itself, one should again grind it with śilā and kāñjika.
Again one should heat it between two earthen saucers; in this way death occurs with sixty heatings.
Into tin melted in an earthen vessel, powder of ciñcā and aśvattha bark,
one should throw again and again, a quarter part, and stir with an iron ladle.
Then, in the space of two watches, tin bhasma is produced.
Now, having added tāla equal to the bhasma, one should grind it with an acid liquid.
Then, after cooking it in a gajapuṭa, one should again grind it with an acid liquid.
Then one should add tāla in a tenth part and heat it for one watch.

children.text: evaṃ daśapuṭaiḥ pakvo vaṅgastu mriyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, cooked with ten heatings, tin certainly becomes dead.
Purified powder produced from iron, with the juices of pātālagaruḍī,
should be ground and heated in fire; in this way one should give three heatings.
There should be three heatings with kumārī, and with the juices of kuṭhāra and kulattha,
one should then give six heatings; in this way the death of tīkṣṇa iron occurs.
Or one should add darada in a tenth part to the powder of tīkṣṇa iron,
grind it with the liquids of kanyakā for two watches, and then heat it.
Thus, with seven heatings, the iron powder obtains death.
With the juices of kuṭhāracchinnā and with the juices of pātālagaruḍī,
with breast milk and with the milk of arka, the death of tīkṣṇa iron occurs in this way.
Having added sulfur twice as much as mercury, one should make kajjalī.
An equal amount of iron powder to the two should be ground with the liquids of kanyakā.

children.text: yāmayugmaṃ tataḥ piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā tāmrasya pātrake ||
children.translated_text: After two watches, having made a lump, in a copper vessel
the wise man should keep it in the sun and cover it with leaves of rubūka.
In half a watch it should become hot; then he should place it in a heap of grain.
Having put an earthen saucer above it, he should take it out at the end of three days.
After grinding it, he should filter it through cloth; in this way it becomes vāritara.
In this way one should kill all metals, even gold and the rest.
All metals, beginning with gold, smeared with śilā, sulfur, and the milk of arka,
die with twelve heatings; this is true, just as the teacher's word says.
Mākṣika, tuttha, abhra, nīlāñjana, śilā, alaka,
and rasaka should be known as these seven upadhātus.

children.text: mākṣikasya trayo bhāgā bhāgaikaṃ saindhavasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Three parts of mākṣika and one part of saindhava
should be cooked with the liquids of mātuluṅga, or with liquids produced from jambīra.
One should stir it in an iron vessel until the vessel
becomes red; then the gold-mākṣika attains purification.

children.text: kulatthasya kaṣāyeṇa ghṛṣṭvā tailena vā puṭet ||
children.translated_text: After rubbing it with a decoction of kulattha, one should heat it with oil,
or with buttermilk or goat's urine; gold-mākṣika becomes dead.
With liquids produced from karkoṭī and meṣaśṛṅgī, and with those from jambīra, for a day
one should impregnate it in strong sunlight; vimalā is certainly purified.
One should grind tuttha with the excrement of cats and pigeons.
Having added ṭaṅkaṇa in a tenth part, one should cook it with a mild heating.
One heating with curds and one heating with honey should be given for the purification of tuttha.
One should blow black abhraka in fire and then cast it into milk.
Having made it into split sheets, with the liquids of taṇḍulīya and sour gruel,
one should impregnate it for eight watches; in this way abhraka is purified.
Having made that into dhānyābhraka and then dried it, one should grind it

children.text: arkakṣīrair dinaṃ khalve cakrākāraṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: with the milks of arka for a day in a mortar and make it wheel-shaped.
One should wrap it with arka leaves and cook it properly in a gajapuṭa.
It should be ground again and cooked again seven times with care.
Then, in the same way, three heatings should be given with decoctions of the aerial roots of vaṭa.
It becomes dead; there is no doubt here. It should be used in all formulations.
An equal amount of ghee with dead abhraka should be cooked in an iron vessel.

children.text: mṛte jīrṇe tadabhraṃ tu sarvayogeṣu yojayet
children.translated_text: When that abhraka is dead and digested, it should be used in all formulations.
Dead abhraka removes death and destroys old age and gray hair.
Joined with appropriate vehicles, it is supreme for removing the corresponding diseases.
Purified dhānyābhraka, combined with musta and six parts of dry ginger,
should be ground with kāñjika for a day with juices produced from citraka.
Then one should give a gajapuṭa; after taking it out from that, one should grind it
in the same way with triphalā water and heat it thus with three heatings.
With the liquids of <s>balā</s>, cow urine, <s>musalī</s>, <s>tulasī</s>, and <s>sūraṇa</s>,
when it has been ground and heated in the fire three times at each time, it goes to death.

children.text: dhānyābhrakasya bhāgaikaṃ dvau bhāgau ṭaṅkaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: One part of grain-like mica and two parts of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>
should be ground, sealed in a closed crucible, and cooked with an intense fire.
The powder, naturally cooling, should be used in all preparations.
Having powdered <s>nīlāñjana</s> and impregnated it with citron juice,
it becomes purified after one day in the sun and should be used in operations.
In the same way <s>gairika</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, cowries,

children.text: taurī śaṅkhaṃ ca kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ śuddhimāyāti niścitam
children.translated_text: <s>taurī</s>, conch, and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> certainly attain purification.
One should cook <s>manaḥśilā</s> for three days with goat urine in a swing apparatus.
One should impregnate it seven times with the bile of a goat; it obtains purification.

children.text: tālakaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā sacūrṇaṃ kāñjike kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having made <s>tālaka</s> into small particles, one should put the powder into sour gruel.
With a swing apparatus for one watch, then with the liquids from gourds,
one should cook it in sesame oil for one watch and in <s>triphalā</s> water for one watch.

children.text: evaṃ yantre caturyāmaṃ pācyaṃ śudhyati tālakam
children.translated_text: Thus <s>tālaka</s>, cooked in the apparatus for four watches, is purified.
One should cook <s>rasaka</s> for seven days with human urine and cow urine.
By means of a swing apparatus purification occurs; then it should be used in operations.
Lac, fish, goat's milk, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, deer horn,
oil-cake, mustard seeds, <s>śigru</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, wool, jaggery, rock salt,
barley, bitter substances, ghee, and honey should be powdered as available.
All metals mixed with these, by a strong fire,
when blown in a crucible, become freed of their metallic essence; there is no doubt.
One should cook it thoroughly in a swing apparatus with decoctions of horse gram and <s>kodrava</s>.
A diamond placed inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber is purified by that for three days.
That diamond, heated again and again, should be quenched with donkey urine.
It should be heated again and quenched again; one should do this three times seven times.
Having ground <s>tālaka</s> with bedbugs until it becomes a ball,

children.text: tadgole nihitaṃ vajraṃ tadgolaṃ vahninā dhamet ||
children.translated_text: one should place the diamond in that ball and blow that ball in the fire.
One should sprinkle it with horse urine and put it back into that ball.

children.text: ruddhvā dhmātaṃ punaḥ secyamevaṃ kuryāt trisaptadhā ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, it should be blown and quenched again; one should do this three times seven times.

children.text: evaṃ ca mriyate vajraṃ cūrṇaṃ sarvatra yojayet
children.translated_text: In this way the diamond is killed; the powder should be used everywhere.
One should put the repeatedly heated diamond into a decoction made from horse gram,
combined with asafoetida and rock salt; after three times seven repetitions it becomes powder.

children.text: maṇḍūkaṃ kāṃsyaje pātre nigṛhya sthāpayet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise man should catch a frog in a bronze vessel and keep it restrained.
Being frightened, it urinates there; one should cast the diamond into that urine.

children.text: taptaṃ taptaṃ ca bahudhā vajrasyaivaṃ mṛtirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: After being heated again and again many times, in this way the diamond is killed.

children.text: vaikrāntaṃ vajravacchodhyaṃ nīlaṃ vā lohitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> should be purified like diamond, whether blue or also red.
It should be sprinkled with horse urine after being heated again and again two times seven times.
Then one should place the ball in the five parts of sheep's milk,
seal it in a crucible heating, and give a heating; one should do this seven times.
<s>Vaikrānta</s> goes to the state of ash and should be employed in place of diamond.
One should steam jewels, pearls, and corals in a swing apparatus
with the fresh juice of <s>jayantī</s>; purification occurs in one watch.
One should quench pearls, corals, and likewise all gems individually
seven times each, when thoroughly heated, with <s>kumārī</s>, <s>taṇḍulīya</s>, and breast milk.
Pearls, corals, and likewise all gems without exception,
of various colors, are killed in a moment; there is no doubt here.
Pearls and corals should be killed as stated for <s>mākṣika</s>.
All gems should likewise be purified and killed as with diamond.
Having collected <s>śilājatu</s> that has oozed from rocks heated by the summer sun,
one should grind it with cow's milk, <s>triphalā</s> decoctions, and the juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
For one day each in the sun, that purified substance attains purity.
The wise man should take the chief <s>śilājatu</s> stone, prepared in small pieces,
put it into very hot water, and keep it for one watch.
Then, after rubbing it, he should take the water filtered through cloth.
Having placed it in an earthen vessel, the learned man should keep it in the sun.
The thick part that is on top should be put into another vessel.
He should keep it in the sun and remove the upper thick part from it.
By taking it again and again in this way, after two months, <s>śilājatu</s>
becomes fit for operations; when thrown into fire it should become like a liṅga.

children.text: nirdhūmaṃ ca tataḥ śuddhaṃ sarvakarmasu yojayet
children.translated_text: It should be smokeless, and then, purified, it should be used in all operations.

children.text: adhaḥsthitaṃ ca yaccheṣaṃ tasmin nīraṃ vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: As for the remaining part that stays below, one should pour water into it.
After rubbing it, one should keep it in the heat and remove it just as before.

children.text: akṣāṅgārair dhamet kiṭṭaṃ lohajaṃ tadgavāṃ jalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should blow iron slag with charcoal of <s>akṣa</s> and, with the water of cows,

children.text: secayet taptataptaṃ ca saptavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: quench it while repeatedly heated, seven times again and again.
Then, having powdered it, with twice as much decoction produced from <s>triphalā</s>,
one should stir it and roast it in the fire; excellent <s>maṇḍūra</s> is produced.
One should kindle dry pieces of wood from a milk-sap tree in the fire.

children.text: nītvā tadbhasma mṛtpātre kṣiptvā nīre caturguṇe
children.translated_text: Having taken that ash in an earthen vessel, one should put it into four times as much water.

children.text: vimardya dhārayed rātrau prātaracchaṃ jalaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: After rubbing it, one should keep it through the night; in the morning one should take the clear water.
That water should be boiled on the fire until everything has dried up.
Then, having scraped it up from the vessel, one should collect the alkali, white in appearance.
When powder-like, it may be applied as a rub; when remaining like a decoction, it may be drunk.
Thus the wise man should use these two alkalis in the appropriate operations.
Mercury is remembered as the conqueror of all diseases and as nourishing.
When it has been prepared on an auspicious day, it brings perfection to both the body and metals.

children.text: rasendraḥ pāradaḥ sūto harajaḥ sūtako rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Rasendra, pārada, sūta, haraja, sūtaka, and rasa:
these are to be known by the learned as its names in operations with <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
Copper, silver, arāra, lead, gold, tin, iron,

children.text: kāṃsyakaṃ kāntalohaṃ ca dhātavo nava ye smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: bronze, and magnetic iron are remembered as the nine metals.

children.text: sūryādīnāṃ grahāṇāṃ te kathitā nāmabhiḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: They are spoken of in order by the names of the planets beginning with the sun.
Having put mercury into a crucible with mustard and garlic, one should bind it firmly.
In a cloth, in a <s>dolikāyantra</s> (swing apparatus), one should steam it with sour gruel for three days.
For one day one should grind <s>sūta</s> (mercury) with liquids produced from kumārī.
Likewise one should grind it for one day with decoctions made from citraka.
In the same way one should grind it for one day with the juices of kākamācī.
The <s>rasa</s> should also be carefully ground with decoctions of triphalā.
Then, after washing the <s>sūta</s> with sour gruel, one should separate it from those substances.

children.text: tataḥ kṣiptvā rasaṃ khalve rasādardhaṃ ca saindhavam
children.translated_text: Then, having placed the <s>rasa</s> in a mortar, and rock salt equal to half the mercury,
one should grind it continuously for one day with lemon juice.
Then mustard, garlic, and chiefly navasādara
in quantities equal to the mercury: with these too the <s>sūta</s> should be ground with rice-husk water.

children.text: tataḥ saṃśoṣya cakrābhaṃ kṛtvā liptvā ca hiṅgunā
children.translated_text: Then, after drying it, making it disk-shaped, and smearing it with hiṅgu,
one should place it in a double earthen-saucer container and fill it with salt.

children.text: adhaḥ sthālīṃ tato mudrāṃ dadyāddṛḍhatarāṃ budhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the wise man should set the lower saucer and apply a very firm seal.
After drying it, he should make fire below and sprinkle water above.
Then he should make an intense fire beneath it for three watches.
In this way one should make the <s>rasa</s> rise upward, free from defects.
Then the excellent <s>rasa</s> attached inside the upper vessel is to be collected.
Having placed ghee in an iron vessel, one should heat it over the fire.
When the ghee is hot, one should add sulfur powder equal to it.
Knowing that the sulfur has melted, one should pour it into milk.
In this way sulfur is purified; it should be employed in all operations.
Cinnabar, impregnated with ewe's milk and with the class of acidic substances,
seven times, carefully, certainly attains purification.
Or, for the duration of one watch, with lemon juice or with juice of neem leaves,

children.text: piṣṭvā daradam ūrdhvaṃ ca pātayet sūtayuktivat
children.translated_text: one should grind cinnabar and sublime it upward, as in the method joined with mercury.
Then, taking the purified <s>rasa</s> from it, one should use it in operations.
Kālakūṭa, vatsanābha, śṛṅgaka, and pradīpaka,
hālāhala, brahmaputra, hāridra, and saktuka,

children.text: saurāṣṭrika iti proktā viṣabhedā amī nava
children.translated_text: and saurāṣṭrika are declared to be these nine varieties of poison.
Arka, sehuṇḍa, dhattūra, lāṅgalī, karavīra,
guñjā, and ahiphena are these seven classes of secondary poison.
Mercury ground with these becomes one whose wings are cut.

children.text: mukhaṃ ca jāyate tasya dhātūṃśca grasate kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: And a mouth arises in it; it devours metals instantly.
Alternatively, pungent alkalis, mustard, the five salts,
garlic, navasāra, and śigru, powdered together,
in equal parts and equal to the mercury, with the liquid of jambīra
or with lemon water or sour gruel, should be thoroughly ground in a warm mortar.
In three days and nights, a metal-consuming mouth appears in the <s>rasa</s>.
Alternatively, <s>rasa</s> should be ground with bindulī insects for three days.
With salts and acids its mouth arises, swift in taking metals.
Now the digestion of sulfur by means of the tortoise apparatus is described.
One should put water in an earthen pot, and in the middle of it a small saucer,
like the lid of a large pot, furnished with a rim in the middle.

children.text: liptvā ca mekhalāmadhyaṃ cūrṇenātra rasaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared the middle of the rim with powder, one should place the <s>rasa</s> there.
Over the <s>rasa</s> one should put sulfur powder in an equal portion.
Having placed a saucer over it, one should apply an ash seal.
Over it one should give a heating with four cow-dung cakes.
Thus, again and again, the wise man should digest sulfur up to six times the amount.
When the sulfur has been digested, the <s>sūta</s> becomes sharp in fire for all operations.
Dhūmasāra, <s>rasa</s>, torī, sulfur, and navasādara:
having made them equal parts, one should grind them with acidic liquids for one watch.
Having placed them in a glass bottle, one should coat it all around with a clay-and-cloth seal,

children.text: vilipya parito vaktre mudrāṃ dattvā ca śoṣayet
children.translated_text: apply a seal at the mouth, and dry it.
One should set the bottle in the middle of a vessel with a hole below.
Filling the vessel with sand up to the neck of the bottle,

children.text: niveśya cullyāṃ tadadhaḥ kuryādvahniṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should set it on a stove and make a fire beneath it gradually.
Then he should gradually kindle a fire somewhat stronger than that.
In this way, in twelve watches, the excellent <s>sūtaka</s> is killed.
When it has cooled by itself, one should break it open and discard the sulfur that has risen upward.
The dead mercury lying below should be employed in all operations.
One should prepare a pair of crucibles from seeds of apāmārga.
In that sealed container one should place <s>sūta</s> mixed with the milk of malayū.
Flowers of droṇapuṣpī, viḍaṅga, and irimedaka:
having put this powder below and above, a seal is applied.
The wise man should join that pellet properly inside a sealed clay-crucible container.

children.text: mudrāṃ dattvā śoṣayitvā tato gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: After applying the seal and drying it, he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> heating.
By just one heating after another, the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes bhasma.
One should grind the <s>rasa</s> a little with the milks of kāṣṭhodumbarikā.
One should prepare a pair of crucibles from asafoetida ground with that milk.

children.text: kṣiptvā tatsaṃpuṭe sūtaṃ tatra mudrāṃ pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed mercury in that sealed container, one should apply the seal there.
The skilled man, having put that pellet into a larger sealed earthen crucible,
should cook it with a gentle heating; the mercury goes to the state of bhasma.
Mercury ground with the juices of <s>nāgavallī</s> and enclosed in a bulb of <s>karkoṭī</s>,
when cooked in a sealed earthen crucible, surely goes to the state of bhasma.

children.text: khaṇḍitaṃ mṛgaśṛṅgaṃ ca jvālāmukhyā rasaiḥ samam
children.translated_text: A broken deer's horn, together with the juices of <s>jvālāmukhī</s>,

children.text: ruddhvā bhāṇḍe paceccullyāṃ yāmayugmaṃ tato nayet ||
children.translated_text: should be sealed in a vessel and cooked on a stove for two watches; then it should be taken out.
One should add an eighth part of <s>trikaṭu</s> and take a niṣka-measure of it,
together with <s>nāgavallī</s> juice; it removes fever caused by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
This preparation is called <s>Jvarāṅkuśa</s> rasa, remover of every fever,

children.text: aikāhikaṃ dvyāhikaṃ ca tryāhikaṃ vā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether one-day, two-day, or three-day fever; there is no doubt.
Mercury, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>tāla</s>, blue vitriol, borax, and sulfur,
all these, equal in quantity and purified, should be ground for a day with the juices of bitter gourd.
With this the physician should coat the inside of a copper vessel,
to the thickness of half a finger; then he should seal its mouth.
He should cook it in a sand apparatus, after placing grains at its mouth.

children.text: yadā sphuṭanti dhānyāni tadā siddhaṃ vinirdiśet
children.translated_text: When the grains burst, he should declare it perfected.
Then, when it has cooled by itself, the physician should take it from the inside of the copper vessel.
Having powdered the rasa called <s>Jvarāri</s> with an equal amount of black pepper,
one should take one māṣa with a piece of leaf; it destroys fever.
In three days it destroys severe intermittent fever, whether quotidian, tertian, or quartan.

children.text: tālakaṃ tutthakaṃ tāmraṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ manaḥśilām ||
children.translated_text: Orpiment, blue vitriol, copper, mercury, sulfur, and realgar
are to be used one karṣa each; one should grind them with water of <s>triphala</s>.
One should place the pellet in a sealed container and carefully give a heating.
Then, having taken it out, one should impregnate it seven times with the milk of <s>arka</s> and with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>,
and again seven times with a decoction of <s>dantī</s> and <s>śyāmā</s>.
A māṣa-measure of this excellent rasa, joined with fifty black peppers,
one gadyāṇaka of jaggery, and two leaves of <s>tulasī</s>,
should be taken faithfully for three days; this supreme enemy of cold is hard to obtain.
The prescribed diet is milk-rice; it is to be given for intermittent fever beginning with chills.
It quickly removes tertian and quartan fevers beginning with burning sensation,

children.text: dvyāhikaṃ satataṃ caiva vaivarṇyaṃ ca niyacchati ||
children.translated_text: as well as two-day and continuous fever, and it checks discoloration.
There should be one part of purified mercury, <s>aileya</s>, long pepper, <s>śivā</s>,
<s>ākārakarabha</s>, and sulfur purified with pungent oil.
The fruits of <s>indravāruṇī</s> are to be four parts in measure.
Together one should grind the powder with the juices of <s>indravāruṇikā</s>.
Having made pills of a māṣa in weight, the learned physician should give them in every fever.
With <s>chinnā</s> juice as the accompanying drink, the pill is regarded as fever-destroying.
Purified, appetite-stimulated mercury should amount to two parts,

children.text: tathā gandhasya bhāgau dvau kuryātkajjalikāṃ tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise two parts of sulfur; one should make a black sulfide mixture of the two.
It should be put into cowries in an amount four times that of the mercury.
After adding one part of borax, one should grind it with cow's milk.
Likewise one should prepare eight parts of pieces of conch shell.
One should put everything inside a heating enclosure between saucers smeared with powder.
Having placed it in a pit a cubit deep, one should heat it with a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out and grind all that together.
Six guñjās of the powder, with twenty-nine peppers,
should be given with ghee in a <s>vāta</s> disorder and with fresh butter in a <s>pitta</s> disorder.
In a <s>śleṣman</s> disorder it should be given with honey, and likewise in diarrhea and wasting,
in loss of appetite, disease of the grahaṇī, emaciation, and weak digestive fire.
<s>Lokanātharasa</s> is beneficial in cough, dyspnea, and abdominal tumors.
After it, one should eat three morsels of rice with ghee.
One should lie supine for a moment on a bed without a pillow.
One should eat non-sour food with ghee and sweet curd.
Generally meat of animals from dry country, cooked with ghee, should be given.
When the digestive fire has arisen, at the evening meal one should give well-milked rice.
In the relishes one should include mung-bean cakes with ghee.
One should bathe him with a paste of sesame and emblic myrobalan, or with ghee.

children.text: abhyañjayet sarpiṣā ca snānaṃ koṣṇodakena ca
children.translated_text: One should anoint him with ghee, and the bath should be with warm water.
At no time should he take oil, nor bilva, nor bitter gourd,
eggplant, <s>śapharī</s> fish, or tamarind; he should avoid exercise and sexual intercourse,
wine, fermented preparations, asafoetida, dry ginger, black gram, and lentils.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ rājikāṃ kopaṃ kāñjikaṃ caiva varjayet
children.translated_text: He should avoid ash gourd, mustard, anger, and sour gruel,
as well as improper sleep and eating from a bronze vessel.
He should avoid all vegetables, fruits, and the like that begin with the syllable ka.
This beneficial <s>Lokanātha</s> should be taken on a day with an auspicious lunar mansion,

children.text: pūrṇātithau site pakṣe jāte candrabale tathā
children.translated_text: on a full lunar date in the bright fortnight, and when lunar strength has arisen.
Having worshiped <s>Lokanātha</s>, he should then feed a maiden.
After giving a gift, the excellent rasa should be taken within two ghaṭikās.
If heat arises from the rasa, then one should take it together with sugar.
One should take the essence of <s>guḍūcī</s>, joined with bamboo manna.
He should consume dates, pomegranate, grapes, and pieces of sugarcane.
In loss of appetite one should give husked grain, fried in ghee and with sugar.
Likewise, in fever one should administer a decoction of grain and <s>guḍūcī</s>.
One should give a decoction of <s>uśīra</s> and <s>vāsaka</s>, together with honey and sugar.

children.text: raktapitte kaphe śvāse kāse ca svarasaṃkṣaye ||
children.translated_text: In <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorder), kapha disease, dyspnea, cough, and loss of voice,
powder of roasted <s>jayā</s> should be given at night with honey.
In sleeplessness, diarrhea, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, and weak digestive fire,
one should drink powder of <s>sauvarcala</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, and <s>kṛṣṇā</s> with hot water.

children.text: śūle'jīrṇe tathā kṛṣṇā madhuyuktā jvare hitā ||
children.translated_text: In colic and indigestion, and likewise in fever, <s>kṛṣṇā</s> joined with honey is beneficial.
In splenic enlargement, abdominal disease, <s>vātarakta</s>, vomiting, and hemorrhoids,
when there is bleeding from the nose and other places, one should administer the juice produced from pomegranate flowers.
For nasal therapy one should give the fresh juice of <s>dūrvā</s>, combined with sugar.
Jujube kernel, <s>kaṇā</s>, and ash of peacock feathers, together with sugar,
should be licked with honey to pacify attacks of vomiting and hiccup.
This procedure, however, should be applied in every <s>poṭṭalīrasa</s>,
in <s>Mṛgāṅka</s>, <s>Hemagarbha</s>, the one called <s>Mauktika</s>, and the others.
Thus this rasa called <s>Lokanātha</s> conquers all diseases.
One should powder ash of cowrie shells and <s>maṇḍūra</s>, and cook them in ghee.
An equal amount of powdered black pepper should be impregnated with betel leaf.
That powder should be licked with honey or else with fresh butter.

children.text: māṣamātraṃ kṣayaṃ hanti yāme yāme ca bhakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: Taken in a māṣa measure at each watch of the day, it destroys wasting disease.
This is indeed <s>Lokanātharasa</s>; after a maṇḍala it removes royal consumption.
One should make thin leaves of gold, fine like birch bark.

children.text: tulyāni tāni sūtena khalve kṣiptvā vimardayet
children.translated_text: Putting those, equal in amount, with mercury in a mortar, one should triturate them.
With the juice of <s>kāñcanāra</s> or with the juice of <s>jvālāmukhī</s>,
or with the juices of <s>lāṅgalī</s>, one should grind it until it becomes a paste.
Then one should add borax there, a fourth part of the gold.
One should also add powdered ground pearls, twice the amount of the gold.

children.text: teṣu sarvasamaṃ gandhaṃ kṣiptvā caikatra mardayet ||
children.translated_text: After adding sulfur equal to all of these, one should grind them together in one place.

children.text: teṣāṃ kṛtvā tato golaṃ vāsobhiḥ pariveṣṭayet
children.translated_text: Then, having made a ball from them, one should wrap it with cloths.
Afterwards, having coated it with clay and dried it, one should place it
inside a covered pair of saucers, and there one should apply the sealing.
One should place that covered vessel in a pot filled with salt.
After sealing it, drying it, and heating it with many cow-dung cakes,

children.text: tataḥ śīte samāhṛtya gandhaṃ sūtasamaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: then, when it is cool, one should take it out and add sulfur equal to the mercury.
Having rubbed it in a mortar as before, one should heat it with a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take it and administer two guñjās.
It may be joined with eight black peppers, or with the three <s>kṛṣṇās</s>.
After considering the doṣas and so on, one single raktikā of the rasa should be given.
Depending on the doṣas and so forth, one should give it with ghee or with honey.
The diet should be made the same as for <s>Lokanātha</s>; the patient should be calm-minded and pure.
This <s>Mṛgāṅka</s> rasa destroys phlegm, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, cough, dyspnea, wasting, and loss of appetite,
as well as emaciation and lack of strength.
One should prepare a paste of gold in the measure of a quarter of the mercury.
Sulfur should be twice as much as those two in its own measure; one should grind it with <s>kāñcanāra</s> juices.
Having made a ball, one should put it in a sealed crucible and then seal it.
The learned physician should cook it in a <s>bhūdharayantra</s> for three days and nights.

children.text: tata uddhṛtya tatsarvaṃ dadyādgandhaṃ ca tatsamam
children.translated_text: Then, having taken all that out, he should add sulfur equal to it.
He should grind it with juices of fresh ginger and with the fresh juice of <s>citraka</s>.
He should properly fill large yellow cowrie shells with that.
From this medicine one should make borax as one eighth part.
Having added poison equal to half the borax and ground it with the milksap of <s>sehuṇḍa</s>,
one should seal the mouths of the cowries with that paste.

children.text: bhāṇḍe cūrṇapralipte ca dhṛtvā mudrāṃ pradāpayet
children.translated_text: Having placed them in a vessel smeared with powder, one should apply the sealing.
Putting it in a pit a cubit deep, one should heat it with a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
When one knows the rasa has cooled by itself, one should administer it as with <s>Lokanātha</s>.
The diet should be understood as with <s>Mṛgāṅka</s>; for three days one should avoid salt.
When vomiting occurs in that patient, then one should give a decoction of <s>chinnā</s>,
joined with honey; likewise, when phlegm is aggravated, one should give <s>uḍa</s> and fresh ginger.
In purgation, roasted hemp should be given together with curd.
It conquers cough, wasting, dyspnea, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, and loss of appetite.

children.text: agniṃ ca kurute dīptaṃ kaphavātaṃ niyacchati
children.translated_text: It also makes the digestive fire blaze and restrains kapha and vāta.
The superior rasa called <s>Hemagarbha</s> should be known as a <s>poṭṭalikā</s> preparation.
There should be four parts of mercury, and the same amount of gold.
Having made a paste of those two, sulfur should be twelve parts.
One should make a black sulfide mixture of these; pearl should be sixteen parts,
conch shell twenty-four parts, and borax one part.
One should grind everything together with the juices produced from ripe lemons.

children.text: kṛtvā teṣāṃ tato golaṃ mūṣāsaṃpuṭake nyaset ||
children.translated_text: Having then made a ball from these, one should place it in a crucible enclosure.

children.text: mudrāṃ dattvā tato hastamātre garte ca gomayaiḥ
children.translated_text: After sealing it, in a pit a cubit deep, with cow-dung cakes,
one should heat it with a <s>gajapuṭa</s> and take it out when it has cooled by itself.
Having powdered it, one should give a measure of four guñjās, combined with cow's ghee.
It is given with twenty-nine unmeasured black peppers.
One should have the patient lick it from a silver, earthen, or glass vessel.
He should follow the same diet as for <s>Lokanātha</s>, with a calm mind.

children.text: kāse śvāse kṣaye vāte kaphe grahaṇikāgade
children.translated_text: In cough, dyspnea, wasting, vāta disease, kapha disease, <s>grahaṇikā</s> disease,
and diarrhea, the golden-wombed <s>poṭṭalī</s> should be used.
Purified mercury, poison, and sulfur should each be measured by one śāṇa.
Seeds of <s>dhūrtā</s> should be three śāṇas; the substance called gold should be twice as much as all of them.
One should carefully make a fine powder of these.
The powder should be given with lemon pulp, in a measure of two guñjās.
Or with the juices of fresh ginger it destroys fever arising from all three doṣas,

children.text: aikāhikaṃ dvyāhikaṃ vā tryāhikaṃ vā caturthakam ||
children.translated_text: whether lasting one day, two days, three days, or recurring on the fourth day.
It also destroys intermittent fever; this famous medicine is called <s>Jvarāṅkuśa</s>.

children.text: daradaṃ vatsanābhaṃ ca maricaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kaṇām ||
children.translated_text: One should take <s>darada</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s>, black pepper, borax, and long pepper,
and powder them in equal parts; this rasa is indeed <s>Ānandabhairava</s>.

children.text: guñjaikaṃ vā dviguñjaṃ vā balaṃ jñātvā prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the patient’s strength, one should administer one guñjā or two guñjās.
Afterward one should have him lick it with honey; the fruit and bark of <s>kuṭaja</s>,
powdered to the amount of one karṣa, conquer diarrhea arising from the three doṣas.
Curd-rice should be given as wholesome food, as well as cow’s ghee and buttermilk.

children.text: pipāsāyāṃ jalaṃ śītaṃ vijayā ca hitā niśi ||
children.translated_text: When there is thirst, cold water is beneficial, and <s>vijayā</s> is beneficial at night.
One should powder together one pala of poison and one śāṇa of mercury.
That powder should be put into a closed vessel made of saucers smeared with glass.

children.text: mudrāṃ dattvā ca saṃśoṣya tataścullyāṃ niveśayet
children.translated_text: Having sealed it and dried it, one should then place it on the hearth.
The fire should be applied gradually for the duration of two praharas.
Then one should open the seal from the upper saucer.
The mercury that has adhered there should be collected slowly and carefully.

children.text: vāyusparśo yathā na syāttathā kupyāṃ niveśayet
children.translated_text: It should be placed in a flask so that there is no contact with air.

children.text: yāvatsūcyā mukhe lagnaṃ kupyā niryāti bheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: As much medicine as comes out from the mouth of the flask when touched with a needle,
that amount of rasa is to be given to one fainted from <s>saṃnipāta</s>.

children.text: kṣureṇa pracchite mūrdhni tatrāṅgulyā ca gharṣayet ||
children.translated_text: After scarifying the head with a razor, one should rub it there with a finger.
Through contact of the blood and the medicine, even one who has fainted lives.
Likewise one bitten by a snake lives even when he is in a state like death.

children.text: yadā tāpo bhavettasya madhuraṃ tatra dīyate
children.translated_text: When heat arises in him, something sweet should be given in that case.
To mercury ash equal sulfur, <s>dhātrī</s>, and realgar should be added.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ pippalī vyoṣaṃ pratyekaṃ śilayā samam
children.translated_text: Copper pyrite, long pepper, and the three pungents should each be equal to the realgar.
One should powder them and triturate them with biles derived from fish and peacock.
After triturating seven times and drying it, two guñjās are to be given; it is beneficial.
After it, one should give the juice of <s>tālaparṇī</s>, or a decoction boiled with the five pungent roots.
The medicine named <s>Jalabandhurasa</s> restrains <s>saṃnipāta</s>.
A water regimen should be observed with it; through that the rasa becomes potent.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ viṣaṃ gandhaṃ maricaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kaṇām
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, poison, sulfur, black pepper, borax, and long pepper
should be ground with the liquids from <s>dhūrtaja</s> for one day and then dried.
This rasa named <s>Pañcavaktra</s>, in a dose of two guñjās, conquers <s>saṃnipāta</s>.
A decoction of <s>arka</s> root with the three pungents should be used as the accompanying drink.

children.text: yuktaṃ dadhyodanaṃ pathyaṃ jalayogaṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: Curd-rice is a suitable wholesome food, and the water regimen should be performed.
Kapha-born disorders subside through this rasa when it is joined with honey.
One should also drink honey and fresh ginger juice after it, for the increase of digestive fire.
Eating ghee and meat as desired, the digestive fire becomes strong.
Mercury, with an equal portion of sulfur, should be ground for one day
with liquids from <s>dhattūra</s> fruits; then one should add an equal amount of the three pungents.
The rasa called <s>Unmatta</s> by name, used as a nasal medicine, conquers <s>saṃnipāta</s>.
One should powder ten niṣkas of skinless <s>jaipāla</s> seed.
One niṣka each of black pepper, long pepper, and mercury should be mixed in.
It should be carefully triturated with liquids from citron for seven days.
This rasa, applied as collyrium, destroys <s>saṃnipāta</s>.
Mercury and borax are equal; black pepper is equal to the mercury.

children.text: gandhakaṃ pippalīṃ śuṇṭhīṃ dvau dvau bhāgau vicūrṇayet
children.translated_text: Sulfur, long pepper, and dry ginger should be powdered in two parts each.
The physician should add husked <s>dantī</s> seed equal to all the rest.
In a dose of two guñjās it is an effective purgative; this great rasa is <s>Nārāca</s>.
It destroys abdominal distension, obstruction of stool, and upward-moving wind.
<s>Darada</s>, borax, dry ginger, and long pepper are each one karṣa.
The drug called <s>hemā</s> should be one pala, and <s>dantī</s> seed should be the same amount.
Having powdered all of them together, one should cook them with cow’s milk.
A purgative dose of three guñjās should be given to patients with obstruction and distension.

children.text: dvau bhāgau hemabhūteśca gaganaṃ cāpi tatsamam
children.translated_text: There are two parts of <s>hemabhūti</s>, and mica is the same amount.
Iron ash is three parts, and mercury ash is four parts.
Tin ash should be three parts; all should be ground together.
Coral and pearl should be added in an amount equal to the mercury.
Trituration should be done with cow’s milk, with the juices of rubbed <s>aṭarūṣaka</s>,
with turmeric water, and with the juice of the plantain tuber,
also with the juice of <s>śatapatra</s> and with the expressed juice of jasmine.
Afterward musk should be triturated with the juice of <s>candratulasī</s>.
This is called <s>Kusumākara</s>, preceded by the word <s>Vasanta</s>.
One should give two guñjās of it with honey; it removes all urinary disorders.
Joined with sugar and sandalwood, it conquers acid-disorder and the like.
There are three parts of mercury ash and one part of gold ash.
One part of incinerated copper, and purified realgar, sulfur, and orpiment
should each be two parts; having combined them, one should powder them.
One should fill cowries with that; borax should be ground with goat’s milk,

children.text: piṣṭvā tena mukhaṃ ruddhvā mṛdbhāṇḍe tannirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: and the openings sealed with it, and then it should be enclosed in an earthen vessel.
When dry, it should be cooked with a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; after it has cooled by itself, one should powder it.
This rasa is <s>Rājamṛgāṅka</s>; in a dose of four guñjās it removes wasting disease.
It should be given with ten long peppers, honey, and twenty-nine peppers,
together with ghee; as regimen, one should avoid women, anger, fire, and exertion.
Or light meats are wholesome, for the pacification of royal disease.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ kuryātkhalvena kajjalīm ||
children.translated_text: Purified mercury and twice as much sulfur should be made into a black sulfide paste in a mortar.
One should grind the sharp powders of the two equally with the juices of <s>kanyakā</s>.
After two yāmas, the prepared ball should be placed in a copper vessel.
Having covered it with a castor leaf, after half a yāma it becomes very hot.
Afterward one should place it in a heap of grain, and after a day and night take it out.
Having powdered it, one should strain it through cloth; truly it will float on water.
One should levigate it seven times with juices of <s>kanyakā</s>, and likewise with those produced from <s>bhṛṅga</s>,
with liquids arising from <s>kākamācī</s> and <s>kuraṇṭa</s>, and with <s>muṇḍī</s> and <s>punarnavā</s>,
and likewise with those born of <s>sahadevī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>nīlī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>citraka</s>.

children.text: saptadhā tu pṛthagdrāvair bhāvyaṃ śoṣyaṃ tathātape
children.translated_text: It should be levigated seven times with each of the separate juices, and then dried in the sun.

children.text: siddhayogo hyayaṃ khyātaḥ siddhānāṃ ca mukhāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the celebrated accomplished formula, received from the mouths of adepts.
It has truly been experienced by me as removing the entire mass of diseases.
In this way one should calcine gold and the others, after powdering them, just as with iron.
Joined with <s>triphalā</s> and honey, it should be employed in all diseases.
With <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, cardamom, nutmeg, and cloves,
these being measured as nine parts, the previous rasa should be equal in amount.
Having powdered it, one should mix it with honey; two niṣkas each are to be eaten.
It is named <s>Svayamagnirasa</s>, cutting off wasting disease and cough.

children.text: pāradaṃ gandhakaṃ śuddhaṃ mṛtalohaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Mercury, purified sulfur, calcined iron, and borax,
<s>rāsnā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and the three pungents,
<s>amṛtā</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, honey, and dry ginger should be powdered in equal parts.
One afflicted with every kind of cough should take three guñjās of <s>Amṛtārṇava</s>.
Half as much mercury and sulfur should be ground for one yāma with juices of <s>kanyakā</s>.
A copper sheet equal to the two should be smeared with the preceding paste.
Having cooked it for one day in a pot apparatus, one should take it out and powder it.
This rasa is <s>Sūryāvarta</s>; at two guñjās it conquers dyspnea.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ mṛtaṃ lohaṃ tāpyaṃ gandhakatālake ||
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, calcined iron, pyrite, sulfur, and orpiment,
<s>pathyā</s>, <s>agnimantha</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, the three pungents, borax, and poison
should be ground in equal parts in a mortar for a day with juices of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>.
Then, for one day with juices of <s>muṇḍī</s>, it is made into pills of two guñjās.
One afflicted with a <s>vāta</s> disorder should eat it; by name it is <s>Svacchandabhairava</s>.
A decoction should be made of <s>rāmā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, dry ginger, and <s>vātāri</s>.
He should drink it warm, with guggulu; it is a pleasant accompanying drink.

children.text: dagdhvā kapardakaṃ piṣṭvā tryūṣaṇaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: Having burnt cowrie shell and ground it with the three pungents, borax, poison,
sulfur, and purified mercury in equal amounts, with liquids from citron,
one should grind it and eat a māṣa; afterward he should lick pepper and ghee.
It destroys disease of the grahaṇī; the suitable diet is beneficial buttermilk and rice.
Calcined copper should be cooked with goat's milk and equal liquids until the liquid is gone.

children.text: tattāmraṃ śuddhasūtaṃ ca gandhakaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: That copper, purified mercury, and sulfur should each be in equal measure.
They should be ground with the fresh juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>; that ball should be sealed for a day.
It should be cooked for one yāma in a sand apparatus; two guñjās are to be consumed.
One should give as the accompanying drink the root of citron mixed with water.
The rasa named <s>Trivikrama</s> drives away urinary stone within one month.

children.text: tālaṃ tāpyaṃ śilā sūtaṃ śuddhaṃ saindhavaṭaṅkaṇe
children.translated_text: Orpiment, pyrite, realgar, purified mercury, rock salt, and borax
should be powdered in equal parts in a mortar; sulfur should be twice the mercury.
Calcined copper equal to the sulfur should be ground with citrons for five days.

children.text: mardyaṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ puṭaiḥ pācyaṃ bhūdhare saṃpuṭodare ||
children.translated_text: It should be cooked with six puṭas in a mountain-shaped sealed crucible.
At each puṭa it should be ground with liquids; all this amounts to six palas.
Two palas of calcined copper and four palas of iron ash
should all be ground for a day with sour citron and cooked with a light puṭa.

children.text: triṃśadaṃśaṃ viṣaṃ cāsya kṣiptvā sarvaṃ vicūrṇayet ||
children.translated_text: Adding poison as a thirtieth part of this, one should powder everything thoroughly.
Mixed with buffalo ghee, one should always eat half a niṣka.
Afterward one should lick a karṣa measure of powdered <s>vākucī</s> with honey and ghee.
<s>Mahātāleśvararasa</s> quickly destroys all kuṣṭha diseases.
Sulfur equal to ash-mercury, calcined iron, copper, and guggulu,
together with <s>triphalā</s>, great neem, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>śilājatu</s>:
having powdered these, one should make each sixteen śāṇas.
One should prepare sixty-four śāṇas of powdered karañja seed.
And sixty-four śāṇas of calcined mica should be stirred with honey and ghee.
Kept in a greased vessel, it should be eaten in a dose of two niṣkas; it removes all kuṣṭha.
This rasa is <s>Kuṣṭhakuṭhāra</s>, preventing suppurating kuṣṭha.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ mardyaṃ kanyādravairdinam
children.translated_text: Purified mercury and twice as much sulfur should be ground for a day with juices of <s>kanyā</s>.
That ball should be confined inside a pot, covered by a copper vessel.
It should be covered with purified sulfur, twice the mercury, with the vessel mouth downward.

children.text: pārśve bhasma nidhāyātha pātrordhvaṃ gomayaṃ jalam ||
children.translated_text: Having placed ash at the sides, then above the vessel cow dung and water
should be added little by little, and it should be cooked on a stove for two yāmas.
Having taken it out after intense heating, when it has cooled by itself, one should powder it.
Wood-fig firewood, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>rājavṛkṣaka</s>,
<s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>vākucī</s> seed should be decocted, and with that it should be levigated.
For one day; the rasa <s>Udayāditya</s> should be given in a dose of two guñjās.
It destroys vicarcikā, ringworm, kuṣṭha, and vātarakta.
As the accompanying drink, powdered fruit of <s>vākucī</s> should be prepared,
cooked down with an equal amount of decoction of khadira.

children.text: triśāṇaṃ tadgavāṃ kṣīraiḥ kvāthairvā traiphalaiḥ pibet
children.translated_text: One should drink three śāṇas of it with cow's milk, or with decoctions of <s>triphalā</s>.
After three days there will be eruptions, or after a week in kilāsa.

children.text: nīlīṃ guñjāṃ ca kāsīsaṃ dhattūraṃ haṃsapādikām
children.translated_text: One should grind <s>nīlī</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, green vitriol, <s>dhattūra</s>, and <s>haṃsapādikā</s>,
together with <s>sūryabhaktā</s> and <s>cāṅgerī</s>, and apply the paste from the root upward.
For the purpose of soothing the place of eruptions, it should be applied again and again for seven nights.
It quickly destroys white <s>kuṣṭha</s>, whether curable or incurable; there is no doubt.
Another application for <s>śvitra</s> too is taught here by the best physicians.
A paste of the powder of <s>guñjā</s> fruit and fire is destructive of white <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Also applied <s>śilā</s> and the ash of <s>apāmārga</s> destroy <s>śvitra</s>.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ caturgandhaṃ palaṃ yāmaṃ vicūrṇayet ||
children.translated_text: One should pulverize one pala of purified mercury with the four aromatics for one yāma.
There should be one pala each of incinerated copper, mica, iron, and cinnabar,
and ten niṣkas each of gold and silver.

children.text: māṣaikaṃ mṛtavajraṃ ca tālaṃ śuddhaṃ paladvayam
children.translated_text: There should also be one māṣa of incinerated diamond and two palas of purified orpiment.
With citron, <s>unmatta</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, <s>snuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, and <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s>,
it is to be ground with liquids born from <s>hayāri</s>, each one day by day.
Thus it is to be ground for seven days; its ball should be wrapped in cloth,
placed in a sand apparatus, and heated for three days with a gentle fire.
Taking it out, one should powder it finely and add one pala of poison,
with two palas of long-pepper powder mixed in. This is the rasa called <s>Sarveśvara</s>.
Two guñjās are licked with honey; it removes numbness, circular eruptions, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
One should finely powder one karṣa each of <s>vākucī</s> and <s>devakāṣṭha</s>.
One should lick it smeared with castor oil; the accompanying drink is pleasant and beneficial.
Having put five palas of the plant called <s>hemāhvā</s> into a pot of buttermilk, one should cook it.

children.text: takre jīrṇe samuddhṛtya punaḥ kṣīraghaṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: When the buttermilk has been absorbed, one should take it out and cook it again in a pot of milk.
When the milk has been absorbed, one should take it out, wash it, and purify it.
Five palas of that powder and two palas of black peppers,
together with one pala of stabilized mercury, should be made into one mixture and eaten.
A patient with numbness and <s>kuṣṭha</s> should take one niṣka; this is indeed <s>Svarṇakṣīrīrasa</s>.
Ash-mercury, incinerated magnetic iron, ash of iron, and bitumen,

children.text: śuddhaṃ tāpyaṃ śilā vyoma triphalāṃ kolabījakam ||
children.translated_text: purified pyrites, realgar, mica, <s>triphala</s>, and jujube seed,
with wood-apple and turmeric powder, should be impregnated with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> juice.
After drying it thirty times, one should always lick it together with honey.
A niṣka measure removes urinary disorders; this great rasa is <s>Mehabaddha</s>.
One should grind the seeds of great neem, six in measure,
with one pala of rice-water and two niṣkas of ghee,
make them into one mixture, drink it afterward, and it destroys long-standing <s>meha</s>.
For four parts of mercury there should be eight of sulfur; turmeric, <s>triphala</s>, and <s>śivā</s>
should each be two parts; <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>jaipāla</s>, and <s>citraka</s>

children.text: pratyekaṃ ca tribhāgaṃ syāttryūṣaṃ dantī ca jīrakam
children.translated_text: should each be three parts; the three pungents, <s>dantī</s>, and cumin
should each be eight parts. One should combine them and powder them.
With <s>jayantī</s>, milk of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, fire, and <s>vātāri</s> oil,
it should be impregnated in order, seven times with each, separately.
The rasa named <s>Mahāvahni</s> should be drunk in a niṣka measure with hot water.
By it purgation occurs; at the end of the day buttermilk-rice with rock salt
should be given as the suitable regimen, and cold water should be avoided.
It is said to remove all abdominal enlargements and is supreme for removing obstructed <s>vāta</s>.
Sulfur, orpiment, pyrites, incinerated copper, and realgar,
with purified mercury, in equal parts, should be ground and impregnated for a day.
It should be impregnated with a decoction of long pepper and with the milk of <s>vajra</s>.
One should eat half a niṣka with honey; it conquers <s>gulma</s>, spleen disease, and the like.

children.text: raso vidyādharo nāma gomūtraṃ ca pibedanu
children.translated_text: The rasa named <s>Vidyādhara</s> is followed by drinking cow urine.

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ hāriṇaṃ śṛṅgaṃ svarṇaṃ śulbaṃ mṛtaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: Borax, deer horn, gold, copper, incinerated mercury,
should be ground for one day with ginger juice, sealed, and cooked in a closed heating.
One should lick one māṣa of the rasa called <s>Trinetra</s> with honey and ghee.
Afterward one should lick rock salt, cumin, and asafoetida with honey and ghee.
It is known to remove colic of digestion, certainly within one month.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ yāmaikaṃ mardayed dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Purified mercury and twice as much sulfur should be ground firmly for one yāma.
Purified copper equal to the two of them should be enclosed in a covered crucible with that mixture.

children.text: ūrdhvādho lavaṇaṃ dattvā mṛdbhāṇḍe dhārayed bhiṣak
children.translated_text: Having put salt above and below, the physician should place it in an earthen vessel.
Then, after cooking it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, he should remove it when it has cooled by itself.
He should powder the contents of the crucible finely; two guñjās on a piece of leaf
should be eaten by one afflicted with every kind of colic, along with asafoetida, dry ginger, and cumin.
One should drink a karṣa of powder made from <s>vacā</s> and black pepper with hot water.
This rasa, <s>Gajakesarī</s>, destroys even incurable colic.
Purified mercury, poison, sulfur, celery seed, and the three fruits,
sodium carbonate, barley alkali, fire, rock salt, and cumin,
black salt, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, sea salt, and the three pungents, in equal quantity,
with <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s> equal to all of them, should be ground with sour citron juice.
One should eat pills the size of black pepper to allay weakness of digestive fire.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ viṣaṃ gandhaṃ samaṃ sarvaṃ vicūrṇayet ||
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, poison, and sulfur, all equal, should be powdered.
Black pepper, in a quantity equal to all of them, with the fruit juices of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>,
should be ground, and the whole should be impregnated twenty-one times.
One should eat a pill of three guñjās to allay every kind of indigestion.
This rasa is <s>Ajīrṇakaṇṭaka</s>; it destroys <s>viṣūcikā</s>.

children.text: mṛtaṃ sūtaṃ mṛtaṃ tāmraṃ hiṅgu puṣkaramūlakam
children.translated_text: Incinerated mercury, incinerated copper, asafoetida, and <s>puṣkaramūla</s>,
rock salt, sulfur, orpiment, and <s>kaṭukī</s> should be powdered in equal parts.
With <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>,
one should grind it firmly for one day with the liquids of bitter <s>kośātakī</s>.
One should lick a māṣa-measure of <s>Manthānabhairava rasa</s> with honey;
then, for the pacification of kapha disorders, one should drink a decoction of neem.
Mercury, gold, diamond, copper, iron, and pyrites,
orpiment, blue antimony, copper sulfate, and opium are to be in equal parts.
One should grind in one part of the five salts,
and, after sealing it below, cook it in an earthen furnace for one day with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>.
One should lick one māṣa of it with ginger juice; it destroys vāta.
As the accompanying drink, one should give a decoction of long-pepper root together with black pepper.
It destroys all vāta disorders, beginning with convulsions.
Gold should be eight śāṇas; mercury is considered to be twelve.
Sulfur too is prescribed as twelve, copper as two śāṇas in measure,
mica should be four śāṇas, and pyrites two śāṇas.
Tin is two śāṇas, sauvīra collyrium three śāṇas, and iron eight;
poison should be made three śāṇas, and <s>lāṅgalī</s> one pala in measure.
One should grind it for one day with juices produced from sour fruits,
give it a mild heating in the fire, and then powder it finely.
A māṣa-measure of the rasa should be given in very severe saṃnipāta,
with fresh ginger juice alone, or with the juice of garlic.
This disease-destroying rasa overcomes vitiligo, all skin diseases, erysipelas, fistula,
fever, poisoning, and indigestion.
Mercury and sulfur should be three karṣas; one should make a black sulfide mixture of the two.
Copper, silver, tin, and lead are each one karṣa.
From <s>śigru</s>, <s>jvālāmukhī</s>, dry ginger, and bilva, and from <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>,
one should perform grinding for one yāma each with their respective fresh juices.

children.text: kṛtvā golaṃ vṛtaṃ vastre lavaṇāpūrite nyaset
children.translated_text: Having made a ball and wrapped it in cloth, one should place it in a vessel filled with salt.
Then one should put the glass bottle in a pot.
After filling it with sand, the fire should be maintained for two yāmas.

children.text: tata uddhṛtya taṃ golaṃ cūrṇayitvā vimiśrayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having taken out that ball and powdered it, one should mix it
with a karṣa of coral powder and a śāṇa-measure of poison.
Likewise one should impregnate it twice with the venom of a black snake.

children.text: tagaraṃ musalī māṃsī hemāhvā vetasaḥ kaṇā
children.translated_text: <s>Tagara</s>, <s>musalī</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>hemāhvā</s>, cane, and long pepper,
<s>nīlinī</s>, cinnamon leaf, cardamom, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>kuṭheraka</s>,
<s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, datura, <s>agastya</s>, and <s>muṇḍikā</s>:
one should grind it with the juices of these, along with madhūka, jasmine, and madana.
After one such processing with each, one should dry and keep it.
With the liquids of citron and ginger, and with sixteen measures of black pepper,
the rasa, measured as two guñjās, is given in cases of saṃnipāta.
This rasa is renowned by the name <s>Saṃnipātabhairava</s>.
Silver, pearl, gold, and lead are each one part,
sulfur is two parts, and mercury three parts; one should grind these
thoroughly with the fresh juice of wood-apple, then put them in a deer's horn.
One should heat it with a medium puṭa; after taking it out, one should grind it
seven times with the juices of <s>balā</s> and three times with the juices of <s>apāmārga</s>.
<s>Lodhra</s>, <s>prativiṣā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>:
with each of these fresh juices there should be three impregnations apiece.
A māṣa-measure of the rasa should be given with honey and also with black peppers.
It destroys all kinds of diarrhea and grahaṇī of every origin.
This rasa, <s>Kapāṭa</s>, kindles the digestive fire in grahaṇī disease.
Calcined mercury and mica, sulfur, alkali of barley, and borax,

children.text: agnimanthaṃ vacāṃ kuryāt sūtatulyān imān sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>agnimantha</s> and <s>vacā</s>: the wise physician should make these equal to the mercury.
Then one should grind them with the liquids of <s>jayantī</s>, citron, and <s>bhṛṅga</s>.

children.text: trivāsaraṃ tato golaṃ kṛtvā saṃśoṣya dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: For three days, then having made a ball, one should dry and keep it.
In an iron vessel one should place a saucer above it and seal it tightly.

children.text: adho vahniṃ śanaiḥ kuryādyāmārdhaṃ tata uddharet ||
children.translated_text: One should make a gentle fire below for half a yāma, and then take it out.
One should add <s>prativiṣā</s> equal to the rasa, and also mocarasa.
With the liquids of wood-apple and <s>vijayā</s>, one should separately impregnate it seven times.
<s>Dhātakī</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, bilva, and <s>guḍūcikā</s>:
after impregnating it with these juices, one should dry it after one processing with each.
One should lick one śāṇa of the rasa called <s>Vajrakapāṭa</s> with honey.

children.text: vahniṃ śuṇṭhīṃ biḍaṃ bilvaṃ lavaṇaṃ cūrṇayet samam ||
children.translated_text: One should powder equally digestive stimulant, dry ginger, biḍa salt, bilva, and salt.
He should then drink it with hot water; it overcomes grahaṇī of every origin.

children.text: tāraṃ vajraṃ suvarṇaṃ ca tāmraṃ sūtakagandhakam ||
children.translated_text: Silver, diamond, gold, copper, mercury, and sulfur,
and iron should be made in progressively increasing measures.
After grinding them with the liquid of <s>kanyakā</s>, one should place them in a glass jar.
One should keep the sealed jar inside a pot surrounded by rock salt.
One should seal the pot properly and then place it on the stove.

children.text: vahniṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ kuryāddinaikaṃ tata uddharet
children.translated_text: The fire should be made very gradually for one day; then one should take it out.
When it has cooled by itself, one should powder it and impregnate it with the milks of <s>arka</s>.
<s>Aśvagandhā</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, <s>vānarī</s>, <s>musalī</s>, and sugarcane,
and <s>śatāvarī</s>: one should impregnate it three times each with their juices.
One should impregnate it with the juices of lotus rhizome, <s>kaseru</s>, and <s>kāśa</s>.
Musk, the three pungents, camphor, cubeb, cardamom, and clove:
one should mix this powder in an eighth part relative to the previous powder.

children.text: sarvaiḥ samāṃ śarkarāṃ ca dattvā śāṇonmitāṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: After adding sugar equal to all of them, one should drink a śāṇa-measure
with two palas of cow's milk, while following a sweet diet.
Through its power, beauty, strength, and brilliance increase.
He may delight many young women, and no loss of semen occurs.

children.text: sūto vajram ahir muktā tāraṃ hemāsitābhrakam ||
children.translated_text: Mercury, diamond, serpent-stone, pearl, silver, gold, and black mica
should each be taken in one-karṣa portions and ground with juices produced from <s>irimeda</s>.
Coral powder and sulfur, two karṣas each, should be mixed in.
Then, after grinding it with fresh juice of <s>aśvagandhā</s>, one should place it in a deer horn,
cook it with a mild heating, and impregnate it with the juices of <s>dhātakī</s>.
<s>Kākolī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, the three <s>balā</s>s, lotus fiber, and <s>iṅguda</s>,
grapes, long pepper, <s>vandāka</s>, <s>varī</s>, and the four <s>parṇī</s>s,
<s>parūṣaka</s>, <s>kaseru</s>, <s>madhūka</s>, and also <s>vānarī</s>:
after impregnating it with the juices of these, drying it, one should powder it finely.
Cardamom, cinnamon bark, leaf, bamboo manna, cloves, aloe-wood, saffron,

children.text: mustaṃ mṛgamadaḥ kṛṣṇā jalaṃ candraśca miśrayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>musta</s>, musk, black pepper, water, and camphor should be mixed in.
With these powders, the rasa called <s>Kandarpasundara</s>, measured by one śāṇa,
should be eaten at night in a śāṇa dose, combined with sugar, emblic myrobalan, and <s>vidārikā</s>.
It should be joined with one-karṣa powder of these and with one karṣa of ghee.
After it, with a steady mind, one should drink two palas of milk.

children.text: ramaṇī ramayed bahvīrna hāniṃ kvāpi gacchati
children.translated_text: He may delight many women and nowhere comes to loss.
One part purified mercury and two parts purified sulfur
should be put in and made into a black sulfide paste; into it one should add powder produced from sharp iron.
Having added an amount equal to the black sulfide paste, one should grind it for one prahara.
Then, in the heat of the sun, one should grind it for three days with the liquids of <s>kanyā</s>.

children.text: tataḥ saṃjāyate tasya soṣṇo dhūmodgamo mahān ||
children.translated_text: Then there arises from it a great emission of hot smoke.
Having made it into a very compact lump, one should place it in a copper vessel.
The wise physician should keep it for three days in the middle of a heap of grain.

children.text: uddhṛtya tasmātkhalve ca kṣiptvā gharme nidhāya ca
children.translated_text: Taking it out from there, putting it in a mortar, and placing it in the heat of the sun,
one should impregnate it three times with the juices of <s>kuṭhāracchinnā</s>.
After drying it in the sun, one should impregnate it three times with decoctions of the three pungents.
It should be impregnated successively three times with the juices of <s>vāsā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>.
Then, having put it in an iron vessel, one should impregnate it with water of <s>triphala</s>,
with <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, pomegranate bark, lotus fiber, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>,
with liquids of <s>palāśa</s> and plantain, and with a decoction of <s>bījaka</s>,
with liquids of <s>nīlikā</s> and <s>lambuṣā</s>, and with juices of <s>babbūla</s> and <s>phalikā</s>.
One should impregnate it three times each, and then with juices of <s>nāgabalā</s>,
with <s>śatāvarī</s> and <s>gokṣura</s>, and with liquids of <s>pātālagaruḍī</s>.
According to availability, one should impregnate it three times each with these medicines.
Then in the morning one should lick a kola-sized dose with honey and ghee.
As its accompanying drink, one should drink a pala-sized dose of decoction of <s>varā</s>.
Used regularly for three months, it destroys wrinkles and grey hair.
This, joined with long pepper and honey, destroys weak digestion, dyspnea, cough,
pallor, kapha, and vāta; there is no doubt.
It conquers gouty blood disease, urinary disorders, <s>grahaṇī</s>, and disease arising in the anus.
When mixed with <s>chinnā</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and honey, it conquers enlargement of the testicles.
It is said to be strength-giving, complexion-giving, virility-producing, and supremely life-promoting.
In time this iron rasāyana conquers all diseases.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ tilatailaṃ ca māṣānnaṃ rājikāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The user of iron should avoid pumpkin, sesame oil,
food made of black gram, mustard, liquor, and sour tastes.

children.text: jaipālaṃ rahitaṃ tvagaṅkurarasajñābhirmale māhiṣe nikṣiptaṃ tryahamuṣṇatoyavimalaṃ khalve savāso'rditam liptaṃ nūtanakharpareṣu vigatasnehaṃ rajaḥsaṃnibhaṃ nimbūkāmbuvibhāvitaṃ ca bahuśaḥ śuddhaṃ guṇāḍhyaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Jaipāla, freed from its covering and sprout, placed for three days in buffalo dung by those who know the juice, cleansed with hot water, pounded in a mortar while still covered, smeared on new potsherds until devoid of oil and resembling dust, and repeatedly impregnated with citron water, becomes purified and rich in virtues.

children.text: viṣaṃ tu khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtvā vastrakhaṇḍena bandhayet
children.translated_text: Poison, however, should be cut into pieces and tied with a piece of cloth.
Having placed it in cow urine, one should keep it in the sun for three days.

children.text: gomūtraṃ ca pradātavyaṃ nūtanaṃ pratyahaṃ budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Fresh cow urine should be supplied every day by the learned.
When three days have passed, one should take it out, dry it, and grind it gently.

children.text: śudhyatyevaṃ viṣaṃ tacca yogyaṃ bhavati cārtijit
children.translated_text: In this way the poison is purified, and it becomes fit for use and pain-removing.
Having cut poison into pieces and bound it in cloth, by means of a swing apparatus
it should be steamed in goat's milk for a yāma; it obtains purification.
But if goat's milk is unavailable, it should be purified with cow's milk.
